Former Vereinigte Alte und Neue Klaus Synagogue in Hamburg

Former Synagogue · Hamburg, Germany

The Orthodox Vereinigte Alte und Neue Klaus moved to Rutschbahn 11 and inaugurated its new synagogue on 28 September 1905. Designed by Semmy Engel, it combined a restrained classical exterior with Art Nouveau interior ornament and accommodated 160 worshippers. During the November 1938 pogrom, the interior was desecrated and destroyed, but the building itself survived. The congregation was forced to sell it soon afterward. It also survived wartime air raids and is now used commercially rather than as a synagogue; the building is not open to the public.
